messages:
alex: Heads-up — we need a compact telemetry contract for GPU backpressure signals across Hosted + Dedicated pools. Goal: one dashboard + alerting surface that both runtime and infra can feed.

maria: Can do. Runtime can emit SM-level occupancy as a gauge per-GPU: `sm_occupancy_pct`. NVML gives SM util-ish but runtime has exact active-warps based counters.

ajun: Obs note: prefer Prometheus-style metrics with these stable labels: `pool_type` (hosted|dedicated), `pool_id`, `gpu_model`, `host`. Avoid raw `tenant_id` to control cardinality — use `tenant_hash` for traceability.

casey: Product asks: what does the console want? Short list: per-pool heatmap (SM occupancy %), queue depth, mem pressure (GB and %), predicted headroom (based on 1-min avg), and per-tier alerts. Drilldown to host-level.

maria: Queue depth needs clarifying: there are two meaningful queues — scheduler queue (requests waiting for a worker) and worker-local queue (requests accepted by worker but waiting for execution). Propose metrics: `scheduler_pending_count` (gauge), `worker_queue_depth` (gauge), `request_queue_latency_seconds` (histogram).

ajun: +1 on histograms for latency. Also export `gpu_memory_used_bytes` and `gpu_memory_total_bytes` so console can compute % and color ramps. For backpressure, add `enqueue_rejects_total` counter with labels `reason=memory|sm_pressure|quota`.

alex: Important: Hosted needs aggregated per-pool rollups; Dedicated needs per-customer (lower cardinality) rollups. We should define an ingestion contract: 15s scrape interval, bucketed histogram metrics, and a JSON telemetry envelope for internal stream consumers. Sample envelope example in case we need logs-pipeline fallback: 

```
{
  "ts": 1766003456,
  "host": "gpu-12.prod.redwood",
  "pool_type": "hosted",
  "pool_id": "hosted-gpu-v2",
  "metrics": {
    "sm_occupancy_pct": 72.5,
    "gpu_memory_used_bytes": 27354124800,
    "scheduler_pending_count": 3
  }
}
```

maria: One caveat: per-request tags (model, route) explode cardinality. Recommend capturing `route_hash` and exporting sampled per-route histograms (1 in 1000) for tail debug only. Full traces remain in APM.

ajun: Naming conventions proposal: `redwood_gpu_sm_occupancy_percent`, `redwood_gpu_memory_bytes_used`, `redwood_scheduler_pending_total` (gauge), `redwood_worker_queue_depth` (gauge), `redwood_enqueue_rejects_total` (counter). Keep `redwood_` prefix to avoid collisions.

casey: UX ask: heatmap rollup should support grouping by `gpu_model` and by `customer_tier`. Also add an SLA scoreboard that tags pools with `expected_tps` so we can surface capacity surprises.

maria: Ownership — runtime: expose metrics + docs; eng-platform: define rollup pipelines and low-cardinality labels; obs (jun): dashboard and alerting queries. Timeline: prototype metrics + dashboard in 2 sprints, alerting policies in sprint 3.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: dashboard "gpu-backpressure-proto" created (draft) — https://grafana.internal/d/gpu-backpressure-proto (auto).

casey: Thanks — @maria @jun can you own owners and open a tracking RFC? I can shepherd console wireframes. :+1: 

maria: Will open RFC today with metric names, sample payloads, and expected cardinality numbers.

ajun: I'll stub dashboard panels and share queries. Also propose we add `30d` retention for these metrics at 10s granularity for capacity analysis.

alex: Great. If we agree on the metric names in that RFC we'll lock the ingest pipeline. Callout: alert thresholds should be set conservatively first (e.g., sm_occupancy_pct > 90% sustained 3m) to avoid noise.

casey: Sounds good. I'll add product acceptance criteria to the RFC.

alex: Closing — thanks all. We'll meet next Tue to review RFC + dashboard draft.
